Write-up:
# Bass–Quillen over regular rings ind-smooth over a Prüfer ring

Claim type: **Literature report**.

There is a substantial established class beyond the elementary one-variable PID case: let $R$ be a Prüfer ring and let $A$ be a **regular Noetherian** ring ind-smooth over $R$. Then every finite projective module $P$ over $A[t_1,\ldots,t_d]$ satisfies
\[
 P\cong A[t_1,\ldots,t_d]\otimes_A P/(t_1,\ldots,t_d)P. \tag{1}
\]
In particular this applies to a smooth algebra over any discrete valuation ring, including a ramified mixed-characteristic DVR. The regularity/Noetherian condition on $A$ keeps this result inside the literal prompt; it is not a claim that an arbitrary regular local ring is ind-smooth over a Prüfer ring.

The deep input is Guo–Liu, *The Bass–Quillen conjecture for torsors over valuation rings*, arXiv:2503.10163v1, Theorem1.8 (=Theorem4.1). For an ind-smooth $R$-algebra $A$ and a totally isotropic reductive group **defined over $R$**, their theorem gives homotopy invariance of the Nisnevich torsor set (also the Zariski torsor set). This is a preprint theorem as checked, not described here as a published result. The retrieved v1 header says13March2025, while its HTML displays an internal August2026 date; the version identifier is the reference boundary.

Apply that theorem with the split group $G=\mathrm{GL}_{q,R}$. Example1.4 includes split reductive groups in the total-isotropic class; for $q=1$ the adjoint condition is vacuous. A rank-$q$ finite projective module has a frame torsor under $\mathrm{GL}_q$. This torsor is Zariski locally trivial by the definition of a finite locally free module. Thus there is no additional generic-triviality hypothesis to verify in this application. The torsor theorem says its frame bundle is pulled back from $\operatorname{Spec}A$, and equivalence between vector bundles and frame torsors gives an isomorphism $P\cong Q\otimes_A A[t_1,\ldots,t_d]$. Restriction along $t_1=\cdots=t_d=0$ identifies $Q$ with $P/(t_1,\ldots,t_d)P$, proving(1).

One must also allow nonconstant rank. A finite projective module has locally constant rank taking only finitely many values; the corresponding pieces are open and closed and are defined by finitely many idempotents of $A$. Apply the fixed-rank argument on each such component, then take the direct sum. Localization at an idempotent preserves an ind-smooth presentation. Rank zero and $d=0$ present no exception.

Here is the finite-presentation reason that the word **ind-smooth** causes no hidden descent gap. Write $A=\varinjlim A_i$ with $A_i$ smooth over $R$, and represent $P$ by an idempotent matrix $e(\mathbf t)$ of finite size. Its finitely many polynomial coefficients descend to some $A_i$. The finitely many coefficients in the identities $e^2-e=0$ become zero at some later stage, by the defining equality criterion for a filtered colimit. At that stage the matrix is an actual idempotent and its image is finite projective. An extension theorem there base-changes to the desired extension over $A$. This argument requires no injectivity of the transition maps, and descending the entries alone without descending the idempotent identities would be insufficient.

The scope includes smooth algebras over an arbitrary DVR because a DVR is a valuation ring and hence Prüfer, and a smooth algebra over a regular Noetherian DVR is regular Noetherian. A localization essentially smooth over the DVR is ind-smooth by expressing the localization as a filtered limit of localizations at single elements. Ramification of the DVR over $\mathbb Z$ does not contradict smoothness **relative to that DVR**.

What remains open is the full statement for a general regular Noetherian base. In particular no blanket extension to every excellent Henselian regular local ring is imported from older literature. Česnavičius, arXiv:2201.06424v4, Section2.1.2(7), explicitly flags the older proof issue for that proposed generality. The present argument relies only on the precisely stated ind-smooth theorem, and does not turn that older claim into a proved case.
